articles.title: Germany: Small plane crashes onto A2 highway, killing 2
articles.summary: Two people have died after a small plane crashed onto Germany's A2 highway near Magdeburg. The crash closed the Hannover-bound lanes on a major east-west route, with no road vehicles reported to be…

image.caption: A small plane crashed into a highway west of Berlin on Friday afternoonImage: Thomas Schulz/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Police in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt said two people were killed on Friday when a small plane crashed onto the A2 highway northeast of Magdeburg, police said.
The crash closed all Hannover-bound lanes on one of Germany's main east-west routes. Police in Magdeburg said initial findings indicated that no road vehicles were involved.
What do we know about the plane crash?
The aircraft came down at around 2:48 p.m. local time (1348 GMT/UTC) between the town of Burg and the Krahenberge highway rest area.
It caught fire, and emergency crews recovered both occupants dead. The cause of the crash was not immediately known.
Photographs showed firefighters extinguishing the remains of a red-and-white aircraft. Its tail lay on the roadway, with burned wreckage on an embankment.
How was traffic affected?
Police and emergency crews remained at the scene. It was unclear how long the closure would last.
The A2 connects the greater Berlin area with Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia, and is a major route for traffic crossing Germany.

articles.title: Gibo: Filipinos will know those defending China’s false narratives
articles.summary: Those defending China and advancing Beijing’s false narratives for the sake of convenience will be made known to the Filipino people, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said yesterday.

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — Those defending China and advancing Beijing’s false narratives for the sake of convenience will be made known to the Filipino people, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said yesterday.
Teodoro said there’s no stopping the public from learning the truth.

“The truth will prevail and (some people’s) credibility will suffer,” he said over True FM, adding China’s good faith and sincerity are put to test by Filipino public opinion due to a transparency initiative.
China defenders, he said, should choose to side with the truth and uphold the arbitral award.
He said it all boils down to the nine-dash line which the Arbitral Award rendered void and with no legal effect.

“If you’re advancing a false narrative for the sake of convenience, the people will know and there will be an accounting someday… I mean, this is a free world. It is an open society so the truth will prevail,” he added.
He labeled as falsehood the statements of the Chinese embassy in Manila and its social media posts.
“That’s unprecedented. We actually are responsible in our messaging. They’re the ones who’ve lowered their level and that is worrisome,” he said.
In managing the situation, the secretary emphasized there is no substitute for the truth. “Let’s stick to the truth, the facts on the ground,” he said.
Teodoro said the Philippines has always been careful in managing differences with China, and expects the same kind of responsibility from Beijing.
He slammed Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s statement that the bilateral relationship was facing “malicious interference” by certain Filipino politicians, describing it as “a threat of censorship.”
New arbitration vs China

Political coalition 1Sambayan is urging the Philippine government to pursue a new round of arbitration against China under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to resolve disputes in the West Philippine Sea.

Citing the 2016 arbitral ruling that favored the Philippines and undid China’s nine-dash line, 1Sambayan said the Philippines can file a case to defend the extended continental shelf west of Palawan, Bajo de Masinloc and Ayungin Shoal.

“What this country should seek from the present contest is not a quieter week at sea but a definitive resolution grounded in law – and such a resolution can come from an UNCLOS arbitral tribunal,” the coalition said on Wednesday.

The convention, 1Sambayan said, would better determine the overlapping claims of China, the Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia in the extended continental shelf in Palawan, rather than any state that has placed the most hulls in the area.
The coalition also demanded that China be held accountable for the damages suffered by Filipino fisherfolk as a result of its efforts to drive them away from their traditional fishing grounds.
It also offered a different legal approach in addressing the continuing standoff at Ayungin Shoal through the installation of a Coast Guard sub-station to enhance maritime law enforcement.
The coalition underscored that arbitration is among the peaceful means every UN member-state can apply to settle disputes.
“This is not an alternative to standing our ground. It is how a country of our size stands it,” said 1Sambayan. “The law is how we keep it.” — Andrew Ronquillo

articles.title: Ex-BARMM lawmaker no-show at PDEA probe
articles.summary: Former Bangsamoro parliament member Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang dodged a summons for him to appear on Thursday before the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), which sought to question him over…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang

MANILA, Philippines — Former Bangsamoro parliament member Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang dodged a summons for him to appear on Thursday before the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), which sought to question him over a suspected half-ton shipment of shabu from Laos worth about P1.5 billion.
Rimbang was identified by the PDEA and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) as an alleged mastermind and financier of the shipment intercepted by authorities in Laos on Oct. 1.

PDEA spokesman Joseph Frederick Calulut said the agency was investigating the shipment’s links to an international drug syndicate believed to be involved in manufacturing and distributing illegal drugs across the Asia-Pacific region.

“We are still looking at this international drug syndicate. This is a large syndicate operating in the Asia-Pacific region, meaning the Philippines is not its only destination,” Calulut told “Frontline sa Umaga” on TV5 yesterday.
Rimbang had earlier denied the allegations in a video posted on Facebook, claiming they were politically motivated because of his ties to the Duterte family.
In a letter dated Oct. 26, he challenged DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla to release evidence supporting the accusations against him.
Other persons of interest summoned by the PDEA include the shipment’s consignee, identified as Abdulkarim Macalatas, and several unnamed individuals.
Calulut said authorities received an intelligence report from a foreign counterpart in September about renewed cross-border drug smuggling.
The information was relayed to the Bureau of Customs (BOC), which later detected suspected illegal substances in the shipment through X-ray screening and narcotics detection dogs.
He said investigators had identified the names listed as recipients but were still determining the identities of the actual consignees, as such shipments commonly use fictitious names.

The shipment was initially supposed to be claimed by its consignee so authorities could arrest the recipient. However, it was declared abandoned after it remained unclaimed within the period set by the BOC, prompting authorities to conduct a physical inspection.
Calulut said investigators had yet to establish whether the drugs seized in Laos and the shipment intercepted in the Philippines came from the same laboratory, although both originated from Laos.

articles.title: Nurse shortage could reach 250,000 by 2030 – CHED
articles.summary: The shortage of nurses could reach 250,000 by 2030 if current figures of 127,000 to 190,000 nurse deficit in 2025 continue, Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Chairperson Shirley Agrupis said…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am

Third year nursing students of University of Perpetual Help System receive their caps and pins during the university's 43rd thanksgiving and commitment rites at Ernesto Crisostomo Palanca Hall in Las Piñas City on June 21, 2023.
STAR / Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — The shortage of nurses could reach 250,000 by 2030 if current figures of 127,000 to 190,000 nurse deficit in 2025 continue, Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Chairperson Shirley Agrupis said yesterday.

In her speech during the ceremonial turnover of the Philippine Nursing Education Roadmap 2020 in Ortigas, Agrupis said that while the Philippines has long been recognized for producing skilled and competent nurses who serve both in the country and abroad, there continues to be a significant lack in the national health care system.

“Estimates cited in the Roadmap place the shortage at 127,000 to 190,000 nurses as of 2025, potentially reaching 250,000 by 2030 if current trends continue. This makes the work of strengthening nursing education even more important,” Agrupis said.
An estimated 200,000 Filipinos live and work in the United Kingdom, including more than 35,000 Filipino nurses serving in its National Health Service.

“We want to continue preparing our nurses for international opportunities through quality education and professional development, while also strengthening our own health care workforce. These priorities must go together,” Agrupis added.
She said the Philippine Nursing Education Roadmap provides the government with a framework.

“The findings point to important areas for improvement: curriculum relevance and clinical preparedness, faculty development, student welfare, institutional resources, research capacity and alignment with workforce requirements,” Agrupis said.
She added that the country currently has 434 higher education institutions offering BS Nursing programs nationwide.
“We must continue addressing differences in resources and capacity to ensure that students across regions receive quality nursing education and adequate clinical preparation,” she said.

Meanwhile, nearly 200 Filipino nurses and careworker candidates are undergoing Japanese language training ahead of their deployment to hospitals and caregiving facilities in Japan under its bilateral labor agreement with the Philippines.
The 198 candidates are the 19th batch under the Japan-Philippines Economic Partnership Agreement and their preparatory training formally opened on Nov. 4.
One hundred twenty-one will attend online language classes, while the remaining 77 will receive face-to-face instruction. The six-month program covers Japanese language, culture and social etiquette.

The candidates will undergo another six months of Japanese language training upon arrival in Japan before beginning their assignments. The training programs are provided free of charge under the government-to-government deployment arrangement.
The candidates will take Japan’s national examination for nurses or certified careworkers while gaining professional experience at Japanese health care facilities. — Christine Boton

articles.title: VP’s SALN, AMLC records formally admitted into evidence
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has formally admitted into evidence the statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN) and Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records of Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte conducts a press conference in Mandaluyong on February 18, 2026.
STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court has formally admitted into evidence the statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN) and Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records of Vice President Sara Duterte, while denying the prosecution’s plea to include Commission on Audit (COA) reports regarding her controversial confidential funds.

In a 21-page order issued Thursday, presiding officer Francis Escudero resolved the prosecution’s formal offer of documentary evidence on Article II (unexplained wealth), defining the exact legal parameters of the trial.

To evaluate the Vice President’s wealth, the court admitted volumes of financial, corporate, tax and property documents dating from 2007 to 2021, overruling the defense’s continuing objection against the use of records that pre-date Duterte’s vice presidency.
However, the tribunal imposed a strict limitation on how these older documents can be used by the senator-judges.
“Records predating June 30, 2022 cannot be used to charge or prove additional, independent offenses committed before the Respondent’s current term as Vice President,” Escudero ruled.

Instead, the tribunal explained that these records are admitted “SOLELY to establish a factual baseline against which the Respondent’s assets, liabilities, net worth, financial resources, transactions and business interests during 2022 to 2025 may be evaluated under Article II.”

On the other hand, it completely excluded all exhibits intended to show that the COA flagged and disallowed disbursements of confidential funds in the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Education in 2022 and 2023.

The court also admitted AMLC intelligence reports, covered transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports involving the Vice President, her husband Manases Carpio and their associated businesses. — Bella Cariaso, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Socmed affecting public perception of VP impeachment
articles.summary: Public opinion of the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte is largely affected by information being shared on social media, a political scientist said.

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am

Political analyst Cleve Arguelles points to a shift in public opinion on Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, citing Momentum Research’s October survey, which found that 39 percent of Filipinos favor her conviction, while 34 percent support her acquittal.
MANILA, Philippines — Public opinion of the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte is largely affected by information being shared on social media, a political scientist said.

In an interview with The STAR’s “Truth on the Line,” political scientist Cleve Arguelles, founder of public opinion research firm Momentum Research, described the ongoing proceedings as the country’s “first social media impeachment trial.”

“Most Filipinos would say that they watch it through clips online, spliced videos. Meaning, our people are seeing the senator-judges using the lens of partisan edits and biased spliced videos. That affects the public opinion as well,” he noted.

Arguelles said less than a majority of Filipinos closely follow Duterte’s impeachment trial, which could mean that the public may be making judgments without being fully informed of the progress of the trial.
“The distractions, the big voices online, that affect their opinion of the trial,” he pointed out.
The latest Momentum survey conducted from Oct. 16 to 19 found that almost four in 10 respondents support Duterte’s conviction.
Asked whether the impeachment court should acquit or convict Duterte on the charge of unexplained wealth, 38.8 percent said the senator-judges must vote to convict.
Some 33.8 percent were in favor of acquittal, while 22.6 percent said they do not know. The remaining 4.7 percent declined to respond.

articles.title: Make Christmas goods affordable, President Marcos tells execs
articles.summary: President Marcos has ordered government officials to make basic commodities affordable this Christmas season, while urging public institutions to keep holiday parties simple as the country prepares…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has ordered government officials to make basic commodities affordable this Christmas season, while urging public institutions to keep holiday parties simple as the country prepares for the effects of a super El Niño.
Marcos gave the directive as he administered the oath of office to 10 ad interim Cabinet officials and agency heads during a ceremony at Malacañang yesterday.

Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, who was among those who took their oath, said the administration is focused on helping Filipino families celebrate Christmas with less worry over rising prices and the cost of daily necessities.

“Hopefully, food prices will continue to drop and, most importantly, Noche Buena will be affordable for everyone. That is the President’s primary instruction,” Recto told reporters in a chance interview at the Palace.

Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon and Public Works Secretary Giovanni Lopez, who also took their oath before Marcos, vowed to strengthen coordination to ease traffic congestion and improve public transportation, particularly during the holiday rush.
Dizon said Marcos wants commuters to spend less time on the road and save on transportation costs, especially during the busy Christmas season.

To accommodate the expected surge in passengers, Dizon revealed that the Department of Transportation plans to deploy additional buses, trains and other public transport services to provide commuters with more convenient and accessible travel options.
Palace press officer Claire Castro, meanwhile, urged government agencies to keep their Christmas parties simple as part of the government’s austerity measures.

“The austerity measures remain in effect to this day. While we are not issuing an order regarding Christmas parties, we would like to remind everyone to keep them simple, as there are still many other pressing issues that we need to address,” she said.

articles.title: Prosecution seeks protection for 55 witnesses in Duterte trial
articles.summary: The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has formally requested judges to provide protective measures to 55 witnesses involved in the crimes against humanity case against former…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Former president Rodrigo Duterte

MANILA, Philippines — The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has formally requested judges to provide protective measures to 55 witnesses involved in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

In a 12-page request originally filed on Oct. 30 and released on Friday, ICC acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said there is an “objectively justifiable risk” that applies to several witnesses and others involved in the case.

“In-court protective measures and special measures are required in order to protect the safety, physical and psychological well-being, dignity and privacy of victims and witnesses that will testify before the Chamber,” read the request.

“Mr. Duterte will not be unfairly prejudiced by the measures requested. The measures sought are proportionate and constitute the least restrictive means necessary to fairly balance Mr. Duterte’s right to a fair and public trial against the Court’s competing obligation to protect the interests of victims and witnesses who appear before it,” it added.

The witnesses were divided into six categories: insider witnesses residing in the Philippines, crime-based witnesses residing in the Philippines, witnesses in the Philippines, witnesses residing abroad, witnesses admitted in the ICC protection program and prosecution staff members.

The prosecution requested three types of in-court protective and special measures for the trial witnesses. These include measures intended to protect a witness’ identity from the public, closed or private session intended to protect particular portions of a witness’ testimony from public disclosure and measures intended to support a witness psychologically during testimony.
Based on the request, the prosecution wanted the protective measures to be in the form of pseudonyms, face and voice distortion and permitted private session.

It said that stringent in-court protective measures for the witnesses “will ensure that they can give evidence freely without fear for their personal safety and without compromising their security or the security of their family members.”
Two witnesses to be presented by the prosecution are its staff members. Details of the nature of their testimony have yet to be released.

For its part, the Philippine National Police is prepared to provide security to witnesses in the crimes against humanity cases against former president Duterte before the ICC, PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said yesterday.
Nartatez said the police have yet to receive any communication from the ICC regarding the protection of the witnesses.
“I do not know who these witnesses are. We have also not received any letter from the ICC,” Nartatez said at Camp Crame.

Meanwhile, National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag said they are hopeful they can arrest Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa anytime soon, with its search unit continuing efforts to locate the senator, who has been in hiding since May.
Matibag said operatives were pursuing leads and verifying information on his whereabouts, but declined to disclose more details .

articles.title: NCRPO warns vs illegal water connections amid El Niño threat
articles.summary: The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) has ordered a crackdown on illegal water connections in Metro Manila, warning that unscrupulous groups are exploiting residents’ need for water…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) has ordered a crackdown on illegal water connections in Metro Manila, warning that unscrupulous groups are exploiting residents’ need for water amid concerns over supply shortages due to the El Niño phenomenon.
The directive followed the arrest of two alleged leaders of groups involved in unauthorized water connections in Baseco compound, Manila, NCRPO officer-in-charge Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano said.
Based on intelligence reports, the two groups allegedly charged residents between P5,000 and P10,000 for installing illegal water lines.

Abrahano directed the five police districts to coordinate with water concessionaires, local governments and barangay officials to identify areas vulnerable to the illegal activity, act on complaints and conduct joint inspections when necessary.
He also ordered investigators to focus on those organizing and financing the operations, including individuals collecting payments from residents.

“We will not allow unscrupulous individuals to take advantage of our people’s need for water, especially during periods when access to this essential resource becomes a serious concern,” Abrahano said.

He warned that unauthorized connections could disrupt water distribution, compromise supply systems and cause financial losses. Residents who avail themselves of illegal connections could also face legal consequences, he added.

With El Niño potentially worsening water supply concerns, Abrahano urged residents to transact only with legitimate water service providers and report individuals demanding payment for unauthorized connections.
The NCRPO said it would continue operations to protect communities from groups profiting illegally from the public’s need for water.
Crop losses

As of Thursday, the ongoing super El Niño has caused an estimated P40.9 million in damage and losses to rice and corn production in the Negros Island Region, affecting 2,353 farmers and 1,483 hectares of agricultural land, according to the Department of Agriculture-Negros Island Region (DA-NIR).

Marion Joseph Tagle, DA-NIR Disaster Risk Reduction and Management chief, said the initial field assessment recorded production losses totaling 1,593 metric tons as of Nov. 5, including 1,366 MT of rice and 195.35 MT of corn.
Rice and corn are currently the only agricultural commodities with reported damage due to El Niño, Tagle said, adding that no livestock losses have been recorded so far.
More severe drought conditions are expected in the coming months, he warned.
Negros Occidental is likely to experience a dry spell in November before progressing to drought from December until March 2027.
Negros Oriental and Siquijor, meanwhile, are forecast to experience drought conditions this month, which are expected to persist until March next year.
Although intermittent rains continue in Negros Occidental, Tagle said the agricultural sector must prepare for worsening dry conditions and possible additional crop losses.
Wildfire prevention

Meanwhile, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources has elevated wildfire prevention to maximum alert status as extreme heat and drying vegetation are expected to create fire-prone conditions across grasslands and forests amid the threat of a very strong El Niño.
Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said regional offices have rolled out measures to safeguard forests and grasslands.

“Our decision to deploy dedicated Bantay Gubat patrols and build firelines in high priority areas reflect our firm commitment to prevent wildfires. We call on all citizens, farmers and local leaders to observe strict bans on open burning and kaingin,” Cuna said.

In Northern Luzon, the DENR Ilocos Region mobilized Bantay Gubat Forest Protection Officers and park rangers to conduct continuous foot patrols in forest conservation areas, National Greening Program plantations and other protected areas.
In Bicol, the DENR is preparing firefighting equipment, training park rangers and barangay officials in basic fire response and integrating El Niño preparedness into local information campaigns.

In Mindanao, the DENR Davao Region temporarily closed the Mt. Apo Natural Park to trekking and recreational activities to allow ecosystem recovery and eliminate the risk of human-induced fires during the peak dry period.
It also intensified patrols to deter illegal logging and detect fire risks in National Greening Program plantations.
The DENR Quick Response Teams remain on 24-hour standby across all regional offices to assist local fire authorities in suppressing wildfires.
“Protecting our forests from fire is a shared national duty,” Cuna said. — Josiah Antonio, Gilbert Bayoran

articles.title: Palace wants deeper probe on Romualdez’s jail ‘assistant’
articles.summary: Malacañang wants a thorough investigation on alleged special treatment for President Marcos’ cousin and former speaker Martin Romualdez after a jail warden admitted that the lawmaker has…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Malacañang Palace, the official residence of the president of the Philippines, as seen from the Pasig River.
Gov.ph

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang wants a thorough investigation on alleged special treatment for President Marcos’ cousin and former speaker Martin Romualdez after a jail warden admitted that the lawmaker has a personal staff staying with him inside the New Quezon City Jail around the clock.

“Right now, we cannot provide a concrete answer, as we do not know the facts – specifically, whether or not he has a special aide. There should be an explanation why there was such arrangement and why on a 24/7 basis. If it turns out to be a form of special treatment, it should not become an accepted practice or norm that should be tolerated,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said Friday at a press briefing.
“However, it would be better to conduct a deeper investigation into why former speaker Martin Romualdez requires a 24/7 aide,” she added.

In her testimony before the Sandiganbayan on Thursday, Supt. Maria Lourdes Pacion told the anti-graft court’s Third Division that she allowed the arrangement because, based on her assessment, “his mental state is not yet that stable.”

“We allow that for human consideration, if the PDL (person deprived of liberty) is not in good condition, because we can’t attend to all their personal needs. We cannot hire any more personnel to assign for the personal needs of Cong. Romualdez,” Pacion said.
She explained that this is not a rare arrangement within detention facilities as it is the prerogative of the jail warden to assess the needs of the PDLs.
Ombudsman warns jail officials
Meanwhile, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said he would conduct surprise inspections at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas to ensure that no one is getting special treatment there.
“Once in a while, at any given hour, whether it be morning or midnight, just to check on everything and make sure that all the rules are being followed in Payatas,” he said.
He said his office will also validate information that Romualdez has an assistant staying with him in his cell, stressing that such arrangement is prohibited.

“We will dismiss them from the service. I will not hesitate. If we find something, we will dismiss them from the service,” the ombudsman said, referring to jail officials who might have allowed such arrangement.
Remulla pointed out that having a personal staff inside the jail could be a “security risk” to the detention facility. — Daphne Galvez

articles.title: VP Sara leaves for Hong Kong
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte left for Hong Kong yesterday where she is expected to stay until Nov. 8, a day before her defense team starts to present evidence in the ongoing impeachment trial against…

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte (front R) leaves court after posting bail in Quezon City, suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte left for Hong Kong yesterday where she is expected to stay until Nov. 8, a day before her defense team starts to present evidence in the ongoing impeachment trial against her.

“The Office of the Vice President respectfully informs the public that Vice President Sara Duterte will travel to Hong Kong from Nov. 6 to 8, 2026, to attend engagements and participate in various activities, including an event organized by the Filipino community,” the OVP said in a statement on Friday.
The OVP added that Duterte was able to secure an order dated Nov. 3, 2026, from the Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98, granting permission for the intended travel abroad.
Duterte is facing a grave threats case before the Quezon City RTC filed by the Department of Justice.

The case against Duterte stemmed from her online press briefing in November 2024 wherein she said that she had hired someone to kill President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez, should she herself be killed.
“Likewise, the Office of the President issued a corresponding travel authority,” the OVP added.
The OVP gave assurance that Duterte will cover the cost of her travel using personal funds. “No government money, resources or facilities shall be used in connection with her travel,” it said.

The Senate impeachment court has been asked by the defense camp to subpoena 24 witnesses for the resumption of Duterte’s impeachment trial on Nov. 9. The names of the witnesses who will testify during whole-day hearings next week have been announced by impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol.
Meanwhile, the OVP denied that it suffered a data leak involving approximately 10 gigabytes (GB) of documents.

The OVP was reacting after cybersecurity advocacy group Deep Web Konek said the alleged data leak surfaced in an underground cybercrime forum, where the hacker, identified as DeathNoteHackers, claimed to have obtained around 10 GB of documents associated with the OVP’s scheduling platform.

“The Office of the Vice President wishes to clarify that the scheduling platform mentioned in recent reports is not a government website,” the OVP said, adding that the platform does not contain confidential government files nor classified government information.
“Therefore, any alleged data leak involving the platform should not be automatically construed as a breach nor compromise of any government information,” it added.

According to the OVP, the “timing and circumstances surrounding the allegations raise concerns that this issue may be part of a broader politically motivated effort to discredit the Vice President and the Office.”

articles.title: Alex Eala outlasts Croatian rival to reach Hong Kong Open semifinals
articles.summary: 'It was a roller coaster for sure and an incredible battle,' says Alex Eala after winning a quarterfinal heart-stopper to march to the last four in Hong Kong

blocks.text: WORLD NO. 17. Filipina tennis star Alex Eala competes at the 2026 Hong Kong Open, her last tournament of the year.
Prudential Hong Kong Open's website
'It was a roller coaster for sure and an incredible battle,' says Alex Eala after winning a quarterfinal heart-stopper to march to the last four in Hong Kong
MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala booked a ticket to the semifinals of the 2026 Hong Kong Open on Friday, November 6, after surviving a thriller against Croatia’s Antonia Ružić, 7-6(7), 7-5.
The two players went neck and neck all throughout, even needing a tiebreaker, where world No. 17 Eala pulled away late from a 6-6 deadlock to take the first set, 7-6(7).
Due to heavy rain, the match also got suspended halfway through the second set, where the Filipina was leading, 4-3.
Ruzic seemingly picked up momentum after the break to take a 5-4 lead. But Eala managed to contain her Croatian foe, winning the last three games to wrap up the match, 7-5.

“It was a roller coaster for sure and an incredible battle,” Eala said of the grueling duel. “I don’t know what inspired me or kept me to continue digging deeper, but Antonia played a really amazing match and I’m blessed to be able to play another round here.”
“When you’re on court, there’s not much else you can think about except how to play right,” Eala responded in her post-game interview when asked how she maintained her composure.
“But I think more than staying focused, it was just choosing to push through and give everything that I have.”
The victory propelled Eala to the last four of the Hong Kong Open for the first time. In last year’s edition, the Filipina star exited in the round of 16 against Canada’s Victoria Mboko.
Eala will face fourth seed Maria Sakkari of Greece in the semifinal round on Saturday, November 7.
The Hong Kong Open is Eala’s last tournament of the year.

The 21-year-old will then mark her homecoming with “Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate” on December 8 at the Philippine Arena in Bulacan, where she is set to face Indonesia’s Janice Tjen. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Police chief condemns ‘terrifying’ Bonfire Night violence across Scotland
articles.summary:
Multiple arrests, emergency services targeted and police van set alight while disorder also erupts in north-east England

A police chief has condemned the “unacceptable and terrifying”…
articles.byline: Severin Carrell, Mark Brown and Jamie Grierson

blocks.text: A police chief has condemned the “unacceptable and terrifying” Bonfire Night disorder that resulted in seven arrests, a police van being torched and an officer and a paramedic being injured in Scotland.

Ch Supt David Robertson of Police Scotland said there had been significant reduction in problems overall, compared with 2025, after the force deployed its largest number of officers since Donald Trump’s visit last year.
However, a police officer and ambulance worker sustained minor injuries after being attacked with fireworks while they were responding to a report of an injured man in Greenside Street, Glasgow.

A police van was then gutted after being set on fire in the same street in the Provanmill area of the city, where a 16-year-old boy was also arrested. In south-west Edinburgh, the Scottish fire and rescue service (SFRS) had to withdraw after trying to put out bin fires set by young local people.

In England, police arrested six people in North Shields near Newcastle upon Tyne after a number of officers were injured, with police and fire service vehicles damaged after fireworks and bricks were thrown at them.
A large group of people had gathered outside a supermarket after wrongly being told it was going to be a house of multiple occupancy (HMO).

As part of Operation Amberlight, Police Scotland had tried to prevent a recurrence of the violence that erupted in Edinburgh and Glasgow last year. Local councils imposed localised bans on fireworks in both cities, with police issuing 21 dispersal orders in Edinburgh and 13 in Glasgow.
“We saw a reduction in serious calls requiring specialist support, with public order officers only being deployed at one location for a yet relatively short period of time,” Robertson said.

“But sadly, we did still see attacks on police officers, firefighters, and the Scottish ambulance service, which is completely unacceptable.” While isolated, the violence seen in some areas was “really terrifying.
He added: “Those who were involved will be identified and brought to justice.”

blocks.caption: Police Scotland mounted its biggest deployment of officers since the visit of Donald Trump last year.  Photograph: Jane Barlow/PA

blocks.text: Mairi McAllan, Scotland’s education secretary, said the emergency services were well-prepared. “The vast majority of displays went ahead without any problems, and that’s to be welcomed,” she told BBC Radio Scotland.
“But nonetheless, I would want to be absolutely unequivocal. Totally unacceptable that any disorder related to fireworks should be ongoing.”

Fireworks were also thrown at members of the public in Clydebank and there were attacks on fire crews in the Knightswood and Castlemilk areas of Glasgow, Cumnock in Ayrshire, Larkhall in South Lanarkshire, and Blackridge, West Lothian.
Police also went to the Kirkton area of Dundee after reports of a significant group of individuals gathering and setting illegal fires.

As part of its Bonfire Night policing operation, Police Scotland had called in assistance from forces in England and Wales, in the biggest deployment of officers since the visit by Trump to Aberdeenshire in 2025. Officers from as far afield as Avon and Somerset, Hampshire, Hertfordshire and south Wales were called up.
after newsletter promotion
The SFRS received more than 800 calls relating to fireworks and bonfires between 5.30pm and 11.30pm on Thursday.

Police said that between Halloween and 5 November they received 1,024 fireworks-related calls. While this was up on the 833 calls received in 2025, police said there had been a reduction in the number of incidents requiring a specialist public order response across the country.

blocks.caption: A number of police officers were injured when emergency services were attacked with bricks, missiles and fireworks in North Tyneside. Photograph: Tom Wilkinson/PA

blocks.text: In north-east England, two men aged 25 and 27, a 27-year-old woman and three teenage boys remain in custody after being arrested by Northumbria police on suspicion of violent disorder.
Ch Supt Daniel Whyte said he anticipated more arrests. “The shocking scenes we witnessed last night were completely unacceptable,” he said.
“Our officers and firefighters were met with violence, including fireworks and bricks being thrown at them and their vehicles. Anyone involved should be expecting a knock on the door.”

On social media, the mayor of north-east England, Kim McGuinness, said: “I’m disgusted by scenes of clearly pre-arranged violence in Meadow Well [North Shields] tonight carried out by a minority of idiots.

“These thugs apparently thought they were attacking a planned HMO, when in fact, it was destined to be a supermarket. This dangerous misinformation and the way it spreads has to be tackled and the stupidity has to stop - there is no excuse for it.”

articles.title: Fact check: Three viral Iran war posts debunked
articles.summary: In the wake of the new US attack on Iran, social media is awash with dramatic images and claims about the fighting. DW Fact Check found AI-generated and recycled videos, as well as misleading posts…

image.caption: Disinformation narratives are often triggered by real news events, such as the latest Iran war escalationImage: U.S. Central Command/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: "The reason we lost is the war," US Vice President JD Vance said, shortly after Republicans suffered major losses during the US midterm elections in both the House and Senate. He was referring to the US-Israel war against Iran.
Hours before the US midterms, the US reportedly struck Iran's Qeshm Island, despite Trump previously saying that there would be no new strikes before the elections.
Among fears of a renewed regional escalation, social media has been flooded with dramatic images and purported battlefield updates. Not all of them are genuine.
DW Fact check takes a closer look at three viral claims.
No Iranian missile drone attack on US aircraft carrier

Claim: In this post on X, a user claims that Iran launched a massive missile and drone attack on a US aircraft carrier, resulting in fatalities. It is accompanied by a video showing an explosion and its aftermath on what appears to be an aircraft carrier. The post has garnered over 643.000 views.

blocks.caption: Hectic camera movements can conceal glitches in AI-generated materialImage: X

blocks.text: Verdict: Fake
The 15-second video is an AI-generated fake.

Although there have been reports of Iranian forces attempting to shoot down a US aircraft, there have been no credible reports of a successful attack on a US aircraft carrier which resulted in fatalities.
The AI video also predates the latest US strikes — it has circulated at least since May this year. At that time, it was shared alongside a different claim unrelated to the current situation.

Frame-by-frame analysis reveals several inconsistencies. At approximately three seconds in, the feet of a running person visually glitch. The sea in the background appears uniform and almost video game-like. At five seconds, several people appear to pass through one another, and their limbs also glitch.

The voices in the audio sound synthetic and appear closely synchronized with the visuals. Both AI Detection tools by Meta AI and Google Gemini identified strong indicators that the video was AI-generated. It is important to note, however, that such tools provide an assessment of likelihood, rather than definitive proof that something was created using AI.
The video is considerably shaky and short, two characteristics that warrant closer scrutiny of possible AI use.
The visual nature of supposedly chaotically filmed videos can cover up glitches that still happen frequently in AI-generated content.
Fact check: How AI videos hijack your emotions in 8 seconds
A burning building in South Korea, not US bases in the Gulf

Claim: This user on X shares a video with the claim that "Iran attacks the US bases in the Gulf." A burning building is visible with large dark plumes of smoke rising from it. It has been viewed over 55.000 times.

blocks.caption: Striking images are frequently recycled to illustrate unrelated eventsImage: X

blocks.text: Verdict: Misleading
A reverse image search shows that the images are recycled and show a fire in South Korea in 2025.

News reports indicated that a fire broke out at a Fashion Logistics Center in Cheonan. The same building is visible in the street-level view of South Korea’s Naver Maps street imagery, and its location matches the red building in a mountainous area which is shown on Google Maps satellite imagery.
Visual cues that match include the building itself, the white lettering "E-Land fashion" on the right side and the mountains in the background.

The reverse image search also reveals that the video has repeatedly circulated. It made rounds in July this year attached to Iran war posts in Tamil and English with one post on X reaching 1.4 million views. Other posts linked it to the war in Yemenand other conflicts, unrelated to the fire in South Korea.
Content farm's posts reach millions
Claim: "Iran has launched a major hypersonic missile attack targeting multiple Israeli military bases," an X account writes. By the time of writing, the post had 2.5 million views.

blocks.caption: Content farms are designed to produce large amounts of cheap, attention-grabbing contentImage: X

blocks.text: Iran claims to have hypersonic missiles and has previously claimed to have fired Fattah-1 missiles at Israel, most recently in June 2025. There are no credible reports about Iranian hypersonic missile attacks during the latest escalation.

The account that has published the claim has over 100.000 followers and posts with high frequency, often over ten times a day. Most of the posts reach hundred thousands of views, often using urgent "Breaking" headlines and repeating similar posts. In one post for example, it claims "the war has officially started" reaching more than 30 million views. These are all hallmarks of a so-called "content farm."

In a comment to DW, analyst Charlene Lin from the internet watchdog NewsGuard writes that this account is a South-Asia based content farm. The account has already been flagged in relation to other disinformation narratives.
Lin writes that such South Asia-based content farms "seem to spread false claims about geopolitics by typically posing as pro-China/Russia/Iran users."
She adds that the account amplifies false claims alongside other accounts that appear to be part of the same network, typically within a short period of time.

Victoire Rio, an expert on social-media monetization and information integrity, wrote to DW that "it's pretty common to see financially-motivated actors from South and Southeast Asia leverage prominent news issues to generate a financial profit off the engagement on platforms like X."

articles.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
articles.summary: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.

blocks.text: A Ryanair flight scheduled to leave Lisbon for Rome on Friday was targeted with a threat, the airline said, while at least 11 flights were targeted in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria, according to AFP.
France also reported at least four of its flights were targeted by threats, however they all landed safely.
No explosives have been found on any planes as of Friday.
As airlines were dealing with this latest wave of threats, several media outlets, including RTÉ, were evacuated after similar warnings were made against them.

Staff at the Irish Independent newspaper and the Dublin offices of radio stations NewstalkFM and TodayFM, were also advised to leave their buildings and UK broadcaster Sky said it also received a security threat.
In a statement, gardaí (Irish police) said they were "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe".
While no link has been established between the threats against airlines and media outlets, the Irish government has warned it is a "likely coordinated campaign of disruption".

In a statement, it said: "Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever. It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralised or co-ordinated effort.
Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin described situation as "worrying" and added his government's first priority was the safety of the Irish public.
"Yesterday, there appeared to be coordinated efforts to disrupt air travel," he said.
Martin told RTÉ it was not yet known if the threats had come from individuals or if it was a "coordinated attack" but said they were being taken seriously.
Ireland is scheduled to host two high-profile European Union meetings in Dublin next week.
Broadcaster Sky confirmed it had received a security threat, hours after RTÉ had evacuated its building.

The broadcaster, which is owned by Comcast, said in a statement read by a presenter on its news channel that the broadcaster had "carried out a security assessment and reported the matter to the relevant authorities".
"The safety and security of our colleagues is our primary concern, and we are working closely with authorities to ensure our people and operations remain secure."
Friday's disruption comes after the Russian extremist group "Male State", named in this week's hoax bomb threats to Italian airports, denied any link to the false warnings.

Replying to the BBC Russian Service, an account on Telegram - one of several linked to the so-called "Male State" and its founder Vladislav Pozdnyakov - mocked any suggestion the group was involved in emailing the threats.

"What Male State? Where have you seen it? It hasn't existed for many years," the message on the channel reads. "If tomorrow they sign a [threat] letter, say, from Putin, will you then try to reach our president to ask your stupid question?"

MANILA, Philippines – Renowned Hollywood actress and humanitarian Angelina Jolie is set to be a guest speaker at the 2026 ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit in Manila on Wednesday, November 11.

Jolie will weigh in on the panel discussion “From memory to possibility: Cambodia, courage and the power of staying.” She will be joined by Cambodian filmmaker Rithy Panh, who survived the Khmer Rouge regime and lived to use his talent for film to spotlight the stories of his people.

The two notably worked together on the film First They Killed My Father, based on the non-fiction book by Loung Ung published in 2000. The film, which premiered in 2017, follows the story of then-five-year-old Ung, who is forced by the Khmer Rouge to become a child soldier.
Jolie had served as director and screenwriter (with Ung), while she and Panh also shared co-producer billing with Ted Sarandos and Michael Vieira.

“Their story is rooted in Cambodia, but its lessons are universal: lasting change is built alongside communities rather than for them; the people closest to a problem are best placed to lead its solution; and real progress for women and families is measured in decades, not project or funding cycles,” the talk’s description reads.
“Those lessons matter well beyond Cambodia: for every economy in ASEAN and for anyone who wants growth to be inclusive, sustainable, and resilient.”

Jolie has long served as a staunch advocate of human rights — her journey dating back to 2000, when a visit to Cambodia to film Tomb Raiders exposed her to the displacement of people across the country. In 2001, she was named the UNHCR Goodwill Ambassador.
She adopted her son, Maddox, from Cambodia in 2002.
She was then granted Cambodian citizenship in 2005 to recognize the “generosity” she has extended toward the country.

Filipina theater star and singer Lea Salonga will also be a featured speaker at the ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit in the interview titled “In unison: Amplifying every voice in ASEAN.” Salonga will share her thoughts on pursuing a creative career in Southeast Asia. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years over 191 murders
articles.summary:
Paul Mackenzie convicted over the deaths of 190 children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families

The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been…
articles.byline: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies

blocks.text: The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.

The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes.

Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran ​a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended.
His accomplices threatened and beat victims to ensure they followed his orders. The emaciated bodies were found scattered in shallow graves and dumped in latrines. Some had been buried alive.
Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast in south-eastern Kenya.
In total, more than 400 bodies have been recovered. Many were severely decomposed and only 26 could be identified.
Mackenzie denied murder charges, saying he did not force the victims to starve, but the court rejected that argument.
The Shakahola tragedy has gripped Kenya since the discovery of mass graves in the forest more than three years ago.
It raised questions about how Mackenzie was able to continue operating despite being on the radar of the authorities since 2017, when police searched his premises.

blocks.caption: Kenyan homicide detectives and forensic experts examine exhumed bodies in Shakahola forest. Photograph: EPA

blocks.text: In 2019, authorities shut down Mackenzie’s church and he relocated ‌to the Shakahola forest, police said.
The case has also led to calls for tougher oversight of churches and other religious organisations in a country where religious faith plays a prominent role in public life.
Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill, describing such institutions as satanic.
Cult members lived in makeshift homes of polythene sheeting and thatch that Mackenzie divided into areas with biblical names such as Jerusalem and Judea.
The plight of his followers began ​to emerge in March 2023, when a man told ​police his brother and wife had starved their children ​to death in the forest on Mackenzie’s orders.

Mackenzie was arrested but released on bail, after which relatives said he brought forward the date ​on which he told his followers the ‌world would end. Police rearrested him and ​started combing through the forest more systematically and began exhuming mass graves.
Last month’s judgment covered 191 deaths while investigations into more than 200 other deaths are continuing.
Justice Kavedza-Mochache said in a hearing lasting more than eight hours that in some cases children were isolated and denied food while their parents watched.
Mackenzie faces other charges over the forest deaths, including those of terrorism, which he has denied.
Prosecutors said that while he was in detention he also directed the deaths of 52 people in Kwa Binzaro village, about 18 miles from Shakahola. Mackenzie has pleaded not guilty in that case.
Reuters contributed reporting

articles.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
articles.summary: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.

blocks.text: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have started to climb following an enormous sell-off on Thursday that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index opened higher following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday.
Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development.
However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September.
The Nasdaq Composite opened up 1.23% and continued to gain in early trading, reversing some of its 5.5% fall from Thursday.
The S&P 500 - home of the largest publicly-traded US companies that are not in the technology sector - also opened up slightly, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average opened a little down.
Firms that experienced heavy losses on Thursday also began to bounce back in early trading.
Nvida, which shed hundreds of billions in market value on Thursday after shares slid more than 9%, began Friday trading up more than 6%.
SpaceX and Tesla shares, which were also hammered on Thursday, saw more mixed gains, up more than 7% and nearly 3% respectively.
The market fluctuations come after the sweeping Democrat victory in the midterm elections.

A number of Democrats campaigned for new rules and regulations for artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres, and the party has since won control of both houses of congress as well as key contests in states that have been part of the AI data centre race.
US President Donald Trump on Friday reiterated his supported for what he calls "super intelligence", saying only "foolish leadership" would "say no to the riches they bring".
However, there have also been concerns over whether the enormous amounts of money being spent on AI will pay off.
As well as the fallout of the midterms and the plunge in artificial intelligence stocks, US traders will also be digesting the latest jobs figures.
And those numbers were better than expected: US employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, well above the average monthly increase and more than double what analysts had expected.
Overall the unemployment rate, which counts the number of people who are out of work but actively looking for a job, eased slightly to 4.1% from 4.2% in September.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the unemployment rate has remained in the narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March.

The increase in jobs was led by the professional and business services sector, which added 70,000 jobs. The healthcare sector added 42,000 jobs, and jobs were also added in transportation and warehousing as well as manufacturing.
Neil Birrell, chief investment officer at investment firm Premier Miton, said while the jobs figures may feel like second billing to the market movements they were still important.
"The US economy is running hard which may mean the risks the markets are worrying about at the moment are not such a risk to the real economy as is being feared," he said.

articles.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

image.caption: The French government is facing not only protests over the rising cost of living but is also grappling with mounting debt costsImage: Lisi Niesner/REUTERS

blocks.text: Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

Germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

As a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.
A barometer of France's public finances
The spread acts as a kind of fever gauge for bond markets, explains Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

"This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide towards a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he explained.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fuelled spending spree to end anytime soon.

"French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE (the French national statistics agency — the ed.), 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.
For more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.
Echoes of the eurozone crisis

France last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how quickly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

The main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and therecent unrest.

The higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

These figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is currently estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Trésor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.
A warning shot for Germany
The trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

"For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warns the Mannheim-based economist.

In France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left La France insoumise (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire." "Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he claims.
'Fairy tales from the left and the right'

For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales." Their common message, he says, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts."
Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.
"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," the expert points out.

"In the past, currency devaluations (of the French franc — the ed.) made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier said.
This piece was originally published in German.
Could France's debt crisis become a problem for Europe?

articles.title: Federal judge temporarily halts building work on Trump’s triumphal arch
articles.summary:
US judge issues 14-day block on construction on DC monument after it was approved by planning commission

A federal judge in the early hours of Friday blocked any construction work from…

blocks.text: A federal judge in the early hours of Friday blocked any construction work from beginning on Donald Trump’s towering triumphal arch for 14 days, a major setback for one of the president’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake the nation’s capital.

The temporary restraining order was issued by US district judge Tanya Chutkan in a Washington DC court that has regularly proved to be a thorn in the US president’s side, such as in previous cases involving election subversion and the January 6 insurrection by Trump supporters.

The new ruling followed a series of steps taken on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the 250ft-high (76 meter) arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a nine-hour hearing where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The arch is one of several projects around Washington that Trump has undertaken as he remakes the city, from renovating one of its storied public golf courses to threatening to demolish the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. Those projects could soon face greater scrutiny after the Democrats gained control of Congress.

The administration had said the work on the arch could begin as soon as the approval and the interior department issued a final decision authorizing construction and the proper notification was published by the National Park Service.

In issuing the delay, Chutkan granted the request of the latest plaintiffs in lawsuits challenging the arch. Chutkan also consolidated lawsuits from the District of Columbia and Virginia with a group of Vietnam veterans and an architectural historian.
It’s unclear how much the project will cost, or how it will be paid for, although some estimates have reached as high as $100m.

blocks.caption: Donald Trump holds up a model for his proposed arch back in October 2025.   Photograph: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The vote by the planning commission on Thursday came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote by the commission broke along federal and local lines. Those in favor work for the administration or are connected to the president, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.

The remote, call-in hearing – which crashed repeatedly in the first few hours and was accompanied by a nearly universally negative comment section – drew witnesses who gave impassioned comments opposing an arch that they said would destroy the solemnity of the nearby Arlington national cemetery, where hundreds of thousands of fallen service members and military veterans are buried.

“In my view, the disruption that the arch will cause to the unobstructed sight line, a symbol of national unity, will disrespect the memory of our veterans,” said Michael Lemmon, a Vietnam war veteran, former ambassador and lead plaintiff in the lawsuit against the arch, in a court filing in February 2026, when the suit was first filed.

“I hope to be interred in Arlington Cemetery alongside my fallen comrades when I pass away. The thought of being interred in the shadow of what I believe to be a personal vanity project is profoundly disturbing to me.”
The panel’s Trump-appointed chair launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Trump for wanting to build it.
“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chair.

As Trump has often remarked, “the great cities around the world have arches: Paris, Rome, London,” said Paoletta, who also serves as general counsel for the White House Office of Management and Budget.

Commissioner Paul Ingrassia, a lawyer for the General Services Administration, said the arch was “not about politics. It’s about remembrance. It’s about celebrating our history. It’s about commemorating veterans. And it’s really something that’s a noble tribute to our nation and something that we can all rally behind.”

But DC city council member Phil Mendelson, who also serves on the planning panel, said the project had not received required approval from Congress, nor had Congress appropriated any money for it. The plan submitted to the commission does not include a reference to military use cited by Trump and other administration officials, Mendelson said.
“We cannot approve final site and building plans until we have the final site and building plans,” he said.
Representative Jared Huffman, a California Democrat who is set to chair the House Natural Resources Committee, called the project ill-advised and illegal.

“This arch would dishonor America,” Huffman told the commission. He called the proposed arch “a tribute to Donald Trump,” not veterans, as Trump administration officials claim. The monument is similar to those built for emperors or kings, Huffman said, adding that Trump was using veterans as a pretext to build a memorial to himself.
The Associated Press contributed reporting
