articles.title: Homes and temples glow across India as Diwali celebrations begin
articles.summary: Millions of Indians will mark the festival of lights with glowing lamps, fireworks and traditional sweets

blocks.text: Millions across India are set to celebrate Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, illuminating homes, temples, offices and streets with oil lamps and colourful lights to symbolise the triumph of light over darkness.
The festival falls on the darkest night of the Hindu lunar month of Kartik, when the moon is not visible in the sky.
Although Diwali traditions vary across India's regions and communities, the festival is widely marked by prayers, family gatherings, the exchange of sweets and the lighting of firecrackers.
But the celebrations come amid growing concerns over air pollution, particularly in northern India.
Seasonal weather conditions and the burning of crop residue contribute to deteriorating air quality, while firecrackers set off during Diwali can make the situation worse.

In the capital, Delhi, the air quality index (AQI) reached 391 on Friday morning, placing it in the "very poor" category ahead of the festival. There are fears that pollution levels could rise further after the celebrations.

India's financial capital, Mumbai, has also experienced high pollution levels in recent weeks, with its AQI reaching 322 on 24 October. Although air quality has improved in recent days to reach "moderate" levels of 104 on Friday, there are concerns that Diwali fireworks could trigger another spike.
In an effort to limit pollution, India's Supreme Court on Monday permitted the manufacture, sale and use of certified "green" firecrackers in Delhi and surrounding areas for a limited period.

These firecrackers are designed to produce 20-30% less emissions than conventional fireworks. But critics have questioned how effective they are in reducing pollution and raised concerns that conventional firecrackers could still make their way into the capital from neighbouring states.

articles.title: Malacañang distances itself from Martin Romualdez aide issue
articles.summary: The Palace on Friday distanced itself from the controversy over former Speaker Martin Romualdez reportedly having staff attend to him while detained at the New Quezon City Jail.

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 6:16pm
The Palace on Friday distanced itself from the controversy over former Speaker Martin Romualdez reportedly having staff attend to him while detained at the New Quezon City Jail.
Following reports that the former speaker escaped from prison, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) confirmed that he was still there — together with a staff member.

“Sa ngayon hindi po tayo ang makakapagbigay ng kongkretong kasagutan diyan dahil hindi po natin batid ang katotohanan kung iyan man ay mayroong special aide. Dapat sigurong malaman at ipagbigay-alam anong dahilan, bakit 24/7, at kung ito ay lumalabas na special treatment, ito dapat ay hindi maging kustombre o kaugalian na nato-tolerate sa ganitong klaseng mga kondisyon at sitwasyon,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a press briefing when asked about the controversy.

(For now, we will not give a concrete answer on that because we do not know the truth if there is a special aide. Perhaps the reasons should be ascertained, if it is 24/7 and if it turns out that there is special treatment, then it should not be customary that these conditions be tolerated.)
Castro said that there should be a deeper investigation into the matter. She said that it was best not to speculate on the matter as more details have yet to emerge.
“Although alam natin na mayroong naka-standby na medical assistance para sa mga nakakulong, hindi po natin batid kung ano talaga ang sitwasyon ni former speaker Martin Romualdez,” she said.
(Although we know that there is standby medical assistance for those jailed, we do not know the situation of former Speaker Martin Romualdez.)
Reports of Romualdez leaving his prison stemmed from columnist Ramon Tulfo, who claimed that he had a source. Tulfo has since retracted the statement, apologizing for his mistake.
Castro lauded Tulfo for stepping up and admitting his mistake.

“Kung nakuryente siya at inamin niya napaka-professional ng kaniyang gesture at sana sa lahat din ng mga nakukuryente at nagpi-fake news sa gobyerno at sa ibang mga liderato natin ay dapat umamin na sila ay mali; minsan kasi sila pa iyong matapang kapag pinupuna mo na mali,” Castro said.

(If he was fed wrong information and he admitted it, his gesture was very professional and hopefully everyone who was fed wrong information and spreading fake news about the government and other leaders should admit that they are wrong; sometimes, the people you admonish for being wrong would still act tough.) —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: What to know about the presidential wiretapping scandal rocking Indonesia
articles.summary: The scandal involves senior members of President Prabowo Subianto's government, and hint at growing tensions among its elites.

blocks.text: Authorities are investigating possible treason in Indonesia after a bombshell announcement this week that President Prabowo Subianto's phone conversations might have been spied on.

Several senior figures of Prabowo's administration have been embroiled in the wiretapping scandal, including his chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - who is not related to the president despite his name.

It is unfolding against what many have interpreted as a widening rift between Prabowo and his predecessor, Joko Widodo - otherwise know as Jokowi - who had thrown his support behind Prabowo's 2024 presidential campaign.
"Listyo's position, as we know, is actually very close to Jokowi," Made Supriatma, a visiting fellow at Singapore's ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute, told BBC Indonesian.
"So now it's practically said that they're going their separate ways."
Listyo Sigit Prabowo, the president's chief of staff, was arrested on Tuesday along with two senior police officers for allegedly wiretapping President Prabowo.

The three men are suspected of keying phone numbers, including Prabowo's, into the police's official electronic surveillance system - which allows authorities to intercept communications - without following proper procedures, such as obtaining an investigation warrant or case report.

Authorities say the operation was discovered last week after a tip-off from a police officer. But they believe the alleged wiretapping stretches back to 2025, when Listyo was serving as the national police chief.
This could amount to treason, as it involved "sensitive information" that could "endanger the interests and sovereignty of the nation", a spokesperson for the president told reporters on Wednesday.
In Indonesia, treason is punishable by life imprisonment or even the death penalty - though the country has not executed anyone in a decade.
The spokesperson said the motive behind the alleged wiretapping remained unclear.

It was not just President Prabowo who was targeted in the alleged wiretapping operation, either. Other targets included politicians, journalists, NGO representatives and businesspeople, authorities said.

On Thursday evening, police named a fourth suspect: Slamet Uliandi, from the national police criminal investigation unit. But he was not detained due to his ill health after suffering a stroke, according to authorities.
Listyo, who was appointed the president's chief of staff last month, was sacked from his new position shortly after his arrest.

This is not the first wiretapping scandal to have involved Indonesia's leaders. In 2014, several wiretapping devices were discovered at Jokowi's official residence when he was the governor of Jakarta. Former president Megawati Soekarnoputri claimed in 2024 that she had avoided using her personal mobile phone number because she was the target of wiretapping.
Indonesia's police chief Suyudi Ario Seto told reporters on Thursday that the probe into wiretapping was "purely law enforcement and has nothing to do with rivalries or anything else".
But many see it as the latest blow in a disintegrating alliance between President Prabowo and former president Jokowi, who led the country from 2014 to 2024.
Jokowi had thrown his support behind Prabowo in the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election, as part of an alliance that ultimately propelled Prabowo to become Indonesia's next leader.
Riding to victory with him was Gibran Rakabuming Raka, Jokowi's eldest son, who became Indonesia's vice president.
Two years on, that alliance appears to be fracturing - even if neither party has confirmed the rift.

Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country.
In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many of Jokowi's allies into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati.

Meanwhile, uncertainty also looms over Gibran, Jokowi's son, who is mired in a growing controversy over the validity of his high school credentials, a pre-requisite to run for vice presidency. He now faces calls to be disqualified from his job, on the grounds that he should not have been eligible as a candidate.

The wiretapping scandal and subsequent arrest of Listyo - who rose to the top of the police force in Jokowi's administration, and is seen as one of the ex-president's longtime allies - is now adding to the tensions between Prabowo and Jokowi.
When asked about the wiretapping incident after the court session on Thursday, Jokowi told reporters that "we should all respect the ongoing legal process".

This latest scandal comes during a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. His flagship free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation.
Experts, meanwhile, say all this has distracted from the more pressing challenges that Indonesians are facing on the ground - from economic uncertainties to environmental pollution.
In recent months, protesters have taken to the streets to pressure the government on a range of issues such as toxic wildfire haze, corruption, and cost-of-living woes.
"It's like we're living in a country on autopilot," Nicky Fahrizal, a researcher at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies in Indonesia, told BBC Indonesian.
"Because the way the government operates proves that it's not the people's interests that are being pursued, but rather the interests of individual groups."

articles.title: Over 100 Chinese deported over alleged POGO links -- BI
articles.summary: The Bureau of Immigration (BI) has deported 115 Chinese citizens who arrested during law enforcement operations against illegal Philippine offshore gaming operators (POGOs) in October.

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 6:04pm
The Bureau of Immigration (BI) has deported 115 Chinese citizens who arrested during law enforcement operations against illegal Philippine offshore gaming operators (POGOs) in October.
In a press release issued Friday, the agency said the deportees were among the individuals arrested in separate operations in Zamboanga Sibugay on October 2, and Quezon City on October 12.

"The deportees, consisting of 62 individuals arrested in Zamboanga Sibugay and 53 in Cubao, are being flown to China aboard a chartered China Southern Airlines flight CZ5308 at NAIA Terminal 3, following the issuance of Summary Deportation Orders by the BI Board of Commissioners," the BI said.

In October, the BI described its anti-illegal POGO operation POGO operation in Zamboanga Sibugay as the country's largest crackdown this year, resulting in the arrest of more than 200 POGO workers, most of whom were Chinese.
Meanwhile, 74 Chinese and two Burmese were arrested in a similar raid in Cubao.

President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. banned all POGOs in the country in 2024, citing their tendency to venture into criminal activities such as financial scams, money laundering, prostitution, human trafficking, kidnapping, torture, and murder.
BI Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado said the ongoing deportation initiative demonstrates the agency's commitment to ensuring that foreigners engaging in illegal activities are held accountable.

"The Bureau will continue strengthening its enforcement operations and coordination with local and international law enforcement partners to combat illegal POGO operations, online scams, and other transnational crimes," the statement read. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Denmark’s top court to rule on ‘parallel societies’ after ‘non-western’ people evicted
articles.summary:
Government claims removal of former residents of housing complex in Helsingør is unrelated to their ethnicity

Denmark’s supreme court is expected to rule on whether the state’s…

blocks.text: Denmark’s supreme court is expected to rule on whether the state’s classification of residents with “non-western” backgrounds is covered by racial discrimination law.

The appeal by residents who were evicted from Nøjsomhed-Sydvej in Helsingør, a city north of Copenhagen, could have far-reaching implications for others who have been forced out of their homes by the controversial legislation previously known as the “ghetto law”. The government now refers to affected neighbourhoods as “parallel societies”.

The residents, who have been unsuccessful in other courts, argue that the evictions by the housing association were intended to cut the number of residents with a “non-western” background in order to stop the area from becoming a “ghetto” and therefore subject to the legislation. The government has previously argued the classification is unrelated to ethnicity.

In December, the European court of justice (ECJ) ruled that the legislation may be unlawful. The law requires housing associations to cut not-for-profit housing by 40%, including by selling or demolishing properties or terminating the lease of tenants by 2030.

It also includes demolishing apartment blocks in areas previously labelled “tough ghettos” (now “transformation areas”) by the government, where at least half of residents have a “non-western” background. Other areas with similar socioeconomic conditions – such as high levels of unemployment or crime – are not subject to these measures.

The policy has been widely criticised by human rights groups including Amnesty International. The European Commission Against Racism and Intolerance published a report last month that said there had been “no positive change in the authorities’ approach to the use of the ‘non-western’ category across various laws, policies and administrative practices, including in relation to the ‘parallel society’ legislation”.

The UN committee on the elimination of racial discrimination has called on Danish authorities to stop using the terms “western” and “non-western” in law and policy, and expressed concern that the parallel societies law has a “discriminatory impact on ethnic minorities”.

Residents in Mjølnerparken housing estate in central Copenhagen, who filed a suit against the law in Denmark in 2020 arguing that using their ethnicity to decide where they can live was discriminatory and illegal, have yet to have their case returned to the domestic courts since December’s verdict. More than 1,000 people were forced to move out because of the law.

But legal experts said that the Nøjsomhed-Sydvej case, to be heard on Friday and Monday, could have implications for the Mjølnerparken case because it is likely to lead to a domestic ruling on whether “non-western” background is covered by racial discrimination law.

Susheela Math, the head of legal at the NGO Systemic Justice, said: “If the supreme court decides that ‘non-western’ background is linked to ethnic origin and racial discrimination law, that raises huge questions for the Danish state.”
It would force the Danish state to decide whether it is to abolish the categorisation entirely, which could have ramifications across society, she said.

“[The government] will refer to ethnic origin when it suits them but inside a court, no matter what you present, they say ‘non-western’ background has nothing to do with ethnicity and that they do not collect ethnic data,” said Math.
It is understood that residents of Nøjsomhed-Sydvej would be allowed to return to their homes if they win the case, expected to be decided later this month.
But it is likely to be much more difficult for residents of Mjølnerparken to return to their homes if they win their case when it is heard, because they have been sold.
The Danish ministry of children, senior citizens, and housing has been contacted for comment.

articles.title: A nuclear reactor inside Pax Silica? DOE says it’s an option
articles.summary: Beyond the nuclear question, critics warn that a Pax Silica deal should be studied well to prevent any exploitative arrangements reminiscent of the Philippines’ colonial past

blocks.text: Beyond the nuclear question, critics warn that a Pax Silica deal should be studied well to prevent any exploitative arrangements reminiscent of the Philippines’ colonial past

items: The Department of Energy is exploring nuclear energy as a potential power source for the Pax Silica industrial hub, which requires an estimated 3,000 megawatts of power.

There are significant regulatory and safety challenges associated with establishing a nuclear reactor, as the Philippine Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority has not yet finalized its licensing and safety requirements.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Getting enough energy was always one of the biggest roadblocks for the power-hungry Pax Silica industrial hub. So what if it went nuclear?

“That’s part of the discussions,” Department of Energy (DOE) Director IV Patrick Aquino told reporters on Wednesday, November 4, when asked whether a nuclear reactor could be located within the envisioned US-backed development in Tarlac.
Aquino said the US side has lined up studies on how to power the hub, although he could not confirm the amounts involved.

“For us, the mandate of the Department of Energy is to ensure that there are energy options, regardless of the location. So it’s just incidental in this case that it’s nuclear,” Aquino said when pressed again on whether a nuclear plant was specifically being considered to power Pax Silica.

blocks.caption: A nuclear reactor inside Pax Silica? DOE says it’s an option

blocks.text: The government has been looking at ways to supply electricity to Pax Silica without burdening surrounding communities. Once fully built, Pax Silica could use an estimated 3,000 megawatts of power. No less than Energy Secretary Sharon Garin has warned that the effect of drawing that much power from the grid itself would be “too dangerous” for the average consumer.
For this reason, the DOE wants businesses locating within Pax Silica to bring their own power, with renewable energy and natural gas also among the options.
But setting up a nuclear reactor comes with its own complications. Aquino acknowledged that regulations governing small modular reactors and micro-modular reactors have yet to be firmed up.
“Since nuclear is heavily regulated, we have to really defer to the regulatory body, PhilATOM, on the necessary licensing as to the site and its safe operation,” he added.

Indeed, licensing and safety requirements have yet to be set by the Philippine Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (PhilATOM), not least because that regulatory agency itself has yet to become fully operational, with leadership appointments and implementing rules still pending.

blocks.caption: A nuclear Philippines in six years? OECD’s nuclear chief isn’t convinced.

blocks.text: The nuclear proposal has already drawn skepticism, some of which surfaced during a Pax Silica forum hosted by Fair Transitions Lab on Wednesday, November 4.

Former UP Diliman College of Science dean Giovanni Tapang told Rappler that building a reactor specifically for the hub could leave the country with expensive, underutilized power infrastructure if the project fails to attract enough investors or electricity demand.
Former Ateneo School of Government dean and environmental lawyer Tony La Viña was similarly wary.

“That’s 10-20 years away. We have no regulatory capacity for nuclear energy, for one. I cannot imagine any nuclear plant of any type being approved any time soon,” La Viña told Rappler. “Of course, there are also the safety and waste issues, both of which we also do not have capacity to address.”
The nuclear discussion adds another layer to scrutinize in the already contentious Pax Silica proposal, which aims to attract advanced manufacturing and semiconductor investments.

At the forum, speakers questioned the project’s massive electricity and water requirements, the extent of technology transfer to Filipino industries, the protection of ancestral lands and affected Aeta communities. (READ: The oil crisis, broken roads, and a resettled Aeta community’s future)

And there may not be much time to settle these concerns before something gets signed. Word has it that Philippine officials are hoping to sign at least a framework agreement for Pax Silica during US President Donald Trump’s expected visit for the 49th ASEAN Summit in a few weeks’ time.
As of November 4, Malacañang said the draft agreement had been sent to the US side for feedback, with no confirmed signing date.

La Viña warned that Pax Silica could end up being reminiscent of exploitative American business arrangements in the Philippines’ colonial past — especially with its terms still out of public view and questions unanswered about who would truly benefit.

“We need to actually see whether or not in this agreement, we are going to regress in time and go back to a time when the Philippines was clearly a colonial subject of the United States,” he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Here’s why persons with disabilities must register under new ID system
articles.summary: The National Council on Disability Affairs targets to register all 2.9 million persons with disabilities under the unified ID system by December 2027, before phasing out the old cards possibly by 2030

blocks.text: The National Council on Disability Affairs targets to register all 2.9 million persons with disabilities under the unified ID system by December 2027, before phasing out the old cards possibly by 2030
MANILA, Philippines – The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) is rolling out a platform where persons with disabilities (PWDs) must register in order to get a new identification card.

It is called the Unified Persons with Disabilities Identification System (UPWDIS), a government system that seeks to eliminate duplication and fraud. It was developed in January 2025 and had a pilot rollout and system testing in August the same year.
The UPWDIS was only formally instituted in June 2026, under NCDA Administrative Order No. 1, and took effect in September.

This system change had to be done after it was found that there could have been as many as 8.5 million “illegitimate” PWDs in the country in 2024, while there were only 1.89 million total registered PWDs at that time.

“The use of the PWD ID has been put in a bad light. There’s always a question of whether it is legit or not, right? That’s why legitimate persons with disabilities, especially those with non-apparent conditions, are doubted,” NCDA Executive Director Glenda Relova said in a mix of English and Filipino, as she held a press conference on Wednesday, November 4.

The NCDA targets to register all PWDs in the new portal by December 2027, before phasing out the old ID cards possibly by 2030. Existing authentic PWD IDs will remain valid during the three-year transition.

The new ID has a standardized template, which includes a QR code and an alphanumeric identification number. According to the NCDA, this would address findings that different ID designs created by local government units (LGUs) are “more susceptible to forgery and counterfeiting.”

The ID card for those with permanent disabilities will have lifetime validity, while those owned by persons with non-apparent disabilities will undergo revalidation every five years. Previously, PWD IDs were generally valid for five years, requiring renewal or revalidation.
The new ID is primarily digital, but physical cards can still be requested.
The photo below shows the look of the new PWD ID.

blocks.caption: Photo from National Council on Disability Affairs

blocks.text: Relova said PWDs must register for the new database through the Persons with Disability Affairs Office (PDAO) in their locality.
She said those with an apparent disability, such as persons who are totally blind, missing limbs, limping, and others, may be registered without a disability certificate.

Those with a non-apparent disability, or disability that is not manifested physically, must have a valid assessment from the PDAO. The PDAO officer will also upload the disability certificate to the UPWDIS.
Relova said the NCDA has conducted training sessions with LGUs to facilitate the registration of PWDs directly into the new system.
The administrative order also specifies that there should be mobile registration teams going to remote, disadvantaged, and underserved areas, in coordination with barangays.
Relova said only the UPWDIS can generate the unique identification number of the new PWD ID.
She said that if PDAO officers are doubting the diagnosis or disability certificate of the applicant, the document would be sent to the NCDA. The council would then verify it with specialists.

Erring government officials involved in distributing PWD IDs to those who are not qualified will also be easily tracked. Relova said only PDAO officers and information technology personnel of LGUs have access to the UPWDIS.

With the new portal, the NCDA can track who encoded the data for the ID of an individual posing as a PWD, who approved the registration, whether the issuing LGU has the capability to print an ID card, and who printed the ID card.
Establishments, merchants, and offices can also verify PWD IDs by scanning the QR code and checking it against the national database through the website https://verify.alaga.ph/.

Previously, establishments had to verify PWD IDs through a Department of Health-managed registry or through the PDAO of the issuing LGU. But the registry was not always updated, making verification difficult.

Since the controversy over fake PWD IDs emerged in late 2024, there have been no individuals slapped with penalties yet, said NCDA Spokesperson Walter Jason Alava. A number of cases are still ongoing.
As of October 2026, there are around 2.9 million registered PWDs, according to the NCDA’s website.
So far, around 1,100 out of 1,642 LGUs have adopted the UPWDIS. Over 190,000 PWDs have been registered under the system, with more than 128,000 digital IDs issued.
Relova recalled that the Senate, during a hearing nearly two years ago, found that the government lost P88.2 billion in revenues due to the proliferation of fake PWD IDs.

She said the funding could have been used for social protection services, such as rehabilitation centers, scholarships to encourage more students to study occupational therapy and speech therapy, and assistive devices for PWDs. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Democrats widen gap in House chamber by flipping more seats, including in Ohio, Arizona and North Carolina; Ted Cruz calls election a ‘Watergate-level repudiation’

blocks.text: Key events

items: 30m agoOpening summary

blocks.text: With the dust still settling on the midterms, attention is already turning to the Republicans who might seek to lead the party into the next presidential race in 2028. JD Vance, Ted Cruz and Ron DeSantis are among those in the mix, as the Republican party begins to reckon with the fallout from its midterms performance.
In this report, my colleague Ariana Baio looks at the early jockeying, the potential contenders and what the midterm results could mean for the party’s future:
Opening summary
Welcome to our live coverage of the US midterm elections – here are some of the latest key developments.

items: A number of closely watched contests in the midterms are still to be called, including the final two US Senate races – in Mississippi and Alaska. The Democratic candidates are hoping to oust Republican incumbents to bolster their new majority in Congress. Right now, Democrats have a 106-seat majority as we await final results.

blocks.text: LIVE next refresh in 60s

items: Democrats flipped another eight House seats, strengthening their majority in the lower chamber. Democrats are now leading Republicans 253 to 157, with 25 races left to call, as a number of GOP representatives felt the weight of the blue wave that has swept their party out of power. Republicans held on to two House seats in the west as congressman Mike Kennedy won re-election in Utah and Amanda McKinney won in Washington.

Democratic socialist Nithya Raman was elected to serve as the mayor of Los Angeles, eking out a narrow win over incumbent Karen Bass, in a major shake-up in local politics that reflects the growing dissatisfaction with the direction of the city. The progressive urban planner had served on LA’s city council since 2020.

blocks.caption: Los Angeles mayor-elect Nithya Raman (centre). Photograph: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

items: Harmeet Dhillon, a key Trump ally, resigned from her position leading the justice department’s Civil Rights division. Attorney general Todd Blanche said he accepted her notice. Dhillon is the first high-ranking justice department official to leave after the midterm elections. Democrats are expected to use their power in taking control of Congress to aggressively investigate executive agencies, including the justice department.

Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic senator-elect in Michigan, said the new majority in the upper chamber needed “action” from their leader. On the campaign trail El-Sayed refused to back Senator Chuck Schumer, who currently serves as the minority leader. Speaking to CNN, El-Sayed reiterated that Senator Chris Van Hollen, the Maryland Democrat, would be an “amazing Senate majority leader”, but didn’t completely rule out supporting Schumer.

Joining the chorus of Republicans who blasted their party’s midterms performance is Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, who said the GOP were handed an “ass-kicking” in losing control of Congress. “It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election, it was a Watergate-level repudiation,” he said on his podcast.

The Nasdaq share index had its worst day in 19 months after slumping 5.5% on Thursday amid growing signs the artificial intelligence industry will face tougher regulation because of the midterm results.
Donald Trump signed a proclamation that preserves the Oval Office and Cabinet Room as national monuments in his first official action after the Republican wipeout.

articles.title: Palace reminds agencies to keep Christmas parties simple
articles.summary: Malacañang on Friday reminded government agencies to keep their Christmas celebrations simple this year, although no order was needed to implement this.

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 5:58pm
Malacañang on Friday reminded government agencies to keep their Christmas celebrations simple this year, although no order was needed to implement this.

In 2025, President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. formally ordered, in a memorandum circular, all national government agencies and local governments to keep their Christmas parties simple in light of the string of natural calamities that struck the country that year.

“Hanggang ngayon po nandoon pa rin ang austerity measures na dapat ipinatutupad. Kaya ang dapat na mga Christmas parties ay hindi man natin ipag-utos, pero ang reminder is dapat na maging simple dahil mas marami pa tayong kakaharapin na mga issues na dapat na matugunan,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a press briefing.

(Until now, the austerity measures are still being implemented. So all Christmas parties, this does not need to be ordered, but the reminder is that things should be simple because we are facing a lot of issues that should be tended to.)
While Castro did not elaborate on what these issues are, the country has grappled with record-breaking oil prices this year due to the Middle East conflict.

After experiencing week-long heavy rains due to the Southwest Monsoon, the Philippines is now being affected by the El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to cause massive dry spells until the first half of 2027. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: 'Several victims' after bus crashes in France, officials say
articles.summary: The local mayor says the bus "left the road and hit a tree in the ditch", with the education minister saying students are involved.

blocks.text: A bus has crashed in eastern France, officials have said, with "several victims".
The incident happened on Friday morning in the town of Lent, north-east of Lyon, around 34 miles (55km) from the border with Switzerland.
The town's mayor Yves Cristin told French media the bus "left the road and hit a tree in the ditch", while the Ain prefecture and education minister said there were "several victims".
French education minister Édouard Geffray said the crash involved students, while transport minister Philippe Tabarot said he was on his way to the scene.
Geffray told reporters his thoughts were with "students involved in the accident" and that it was "always difficult when our children are victims of accidents of this nature".
Photos circulating in French media show a blue and white bus tilted in what appears to be a ditch on the roadside. Trees line the side of the road.
The front of the bus appears to be heavily damaged.
Emergency services are at the scene and a helicopter has been deployed to take victims with serious injuries to a specialised hospital.
Cristin told French media two people were in cardiac arrest.
The crash happened at around 07:00 local time (06:00 GMT).

articles.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
articles.summary: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.

blocks.text: Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk says.
He did not spell out whether it plans to stop making them entirely or shift production elsewhere, but did say the decision was to "make room" for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars.

But the project's lead engineer, Wes Morrill, appeared to suggest the vehicle was being discontinued, writing on X: "Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab."
With its distinctive angular looks, the Cybertruck attracted diehard fans, but was beset by delays before being launched in 2023 and has had disappointing sales numbers since.
Tesla fans have been mourning the news online, with one person calling it "the best vehicle Tesla has ever made, external" as he lamented it being "discontinued next year".
Musk responded to the user, external with the word "true", adding: "But the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time."

The vehicle has always been a passion project for Musk. He said it was "way more awesome than people realise, external" in March, and called it the "best product Tesla has ever made to date, external" in April.
But there have always been big questions about whether consumers shared that view and whether the Cybertruck could cut through and earn a spot in the US' lucrative truck market.
It was not helped by inauspicious introduction to the public in 2019 when Musk attempted to show off the Cybertruck's apparently unbreakable glass, only for it to shatter during a live demonstration.

articles.title: Low pressure in US midwest brings unseasonable heat to New York and Boston
articles.summary:
Further south this week, severe thunderstorms affected midterms voting in Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado

Despite the rapid descent into autumn in the northern hemisphere, parts of eastern…

blocks.text: Despite the rapid descent into autumn in the northern hemisphere, parts of eastern North America have experienced an exceptionally late taste of summer in recent days. Temperatures approached 23C (73.4F) in New York and Boston, about 7-10C above what is expected in early November. The unseasonable warmth also spilled into parts of eastern Canada, with temperatures exceeding 20C, about 10-15C above normal for the time of year. The balmy conditions were the result on an area of low pressure in the US midwest, dragging up exceptionally warm air from the Gulf of Mexico along its eastern flank. This area of low pressure will gradually drift eastwards, allowing temperatures to fall closer to the average.

Further south in the US, severe thunderstorms have resulted in numerous flood warnings and evacuation warnings being issued this week across many states, with disruptive weather impacting polling stations in states such Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado. The powerful thunderstorms this week even resulted in a tornado touching down in Keyes, Oklahoma, forcing a relocation of the polling station. The tornado left extensive damage across the town, although no causalities have been reported. Officials across many states impacted by the severe weather have requested federal funding assistance after extreme weather resulted in widespread damage to homes and infrastructure.

Across the Atlantic, a number of authorities in the Mediterranean regions of southern France, Corsica and Sardinia issued severe flood warnings this week, as an area of low pressure in the region brought thunderstorms and torrential rain. As much as 50-100mm (2-4in) of rain is expected over the coming days with more localised totals in excess of 100mm possible in the southern French regions of Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur and Occitanie, as well as Corsica. Where torrential rain is most prolonged, up to 70-80mm of rain could fall within a 24-hour period. Further rain is expected next week as low pressure continues to dominate the weather pattern in the region.

articles.title: Ombudsman eyes charges vs. fake news peddlers claiming he is sick
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Friday vowed to go after Facebook pages that identify him as someone afflicted with leukemia, saying he has been cancer-free for three years now.

blocks.text: Filtered By: Topstories
News
Published November 6, 2026 5:42pm
"It's been almost three years since I've been cancer-free, yet some still want to spread false information and weaken our office,” Remulla said. (Screenshot from Ombudsman press con video)
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Friday vowed to go after Facebook pages that identify him as someone afflicted with leukemia, saying he has been cancer-free for three years now.

“There's been a lot of fake news lately. [There are] people who are trying to create doubt about the office [of the Ombudsman] or maybe even the state of my health. This has to stop, and we are filing a complaint with DICT and Facebook itself to stop the proliferation of fake news,” Remulla said in a press conference.
He was referring to one of his previous illnesses, including one when he had to undergo a heart bypass operation in 2023.

“If you look through the interviews I gave about what I went through, I think it's obvious that it's already over. I was alarmed because I received the texts from people in media, my friends, saying that they're praying for me,” Remulla said.

“I said thank you, but my answer is, it's been almost three years since I've been cancer-free [and yet there are those who] still want to spread false information and weaken our office,” Remulla added.
Remulla said social media is being used by his detractors, such as the supporters of the Duterte family or those who are facing charges over the flood control mess.

“Obviously, it's meant to influence people so that they will have doubts about our government and this office. That's one of the things that I wanted to address today. They're trying to deceive people by having all of these social media articles that actually do not reflect the truth or the full truth,” Remulla said. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Ombudsman Remulla: Romualdez cannot have personal staff with him in jail
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Friday said they will verify the information concerning former Speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez being accompanied by a personal staff while in…

blocks.text: SETS SURPRISE VISITS TO PAYATAS JAIL
Published November 6, 2026 5:37pm

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Friday said they will verify the information concerning former Speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez being accompanied by a personal staff while in detention in a Quezon City jail over a P7.4-billion plunder charge.

Remulla made the announcement a day after BJMP Jail Warden Lourdes Pacion told the Sandiganbayan that a personal staff of former Speaker is staying with the lawmaker in his cell in the New Quezon City jail.

Pacion made the testimony during the hearing on the status of Romualdez's detention amid allegations of columnist Ramon Tulfo that the former speaker is able to leave the BJMP facility as he pleases in an ambulance.
Tulfo, however, has since retracted on his claims.

“To remove any doubt about how things are going, we will do surprise visits to jail. We will visit Payatas, at any given hour, whether it be morning or it's midnight, just to check on everything and make sure that all the rules are being followed,” Remulla said at a press conference.

“We will have to validate it (Romualdez having a personal staff. We don't want special treatment for anybody. Him having a PA, ngayon ko lang narinig iyon eh. Kaya lalo ako nagagalit ‘pag ganun e. Hindi puwede ‘yun. (I learned about it only now ... that's why I'm mad about it and it is not allowed) Blindsided ako run,” Remulla added.
Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, the Ombudsman’s brother, earlier said that the personal staff is a visitor who comes in and out on certain hours only.
Ombudsman Remulla then maintained that a person deprived of liberty having a personal staff by his bedside is not allowed and is an unlawful favor.
“Bawal yan. That’s favoring somebody,” the Ombudsman said.
(That is not allowed.)

Romualdez is one of the accused in the P7.4 billion plunder charge alongside former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, his personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Sereño, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation over their alleged involvement in the flood control mess.

The former Speaker has maintained that he is innocent of the charges and is ready to defend himself by taking the witness stand once the defense presents its evidence in his bail hearing. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Padilla envies Bato dela Rosa for being 'wanted' by ICC, won't ask him to surrender
articles.summary: Senator Robin Padilla said Friday that he envies Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is currently in hiding, for being wanted by a foreign institution, referring to the International Criminal Court…

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 5:34pm

Senator Robin Padilla said Friday that he envies Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is currently in hiding, for being wanted by a foreign institution, referring to the International Criminal Court (ICC).
Dela Rosa has a pending arrest warrant from the ICC in relation to the drug war of former president Rodrigo Duterte, during which Dela Rosa served as chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP).
“Message ko kay kumpare ko? Siguro gusto ko malaman mo naiinggit ako sa’yo. ‘Yun lang, naiinggit ako… Aba eh dayuhan ang naghahanap sa kaniya, eh sa akin...,” Padilla told reporters.
(My message to him? I guess I want you to know that I envy you. That's all—I envy you… Why? A foreign institution is looking for him, while as for me...)

“Ganito lang ‘yan, bigyan ko kayo ng ano. Nung binitay si [Macario] Sakay, masarap ang pakiramdam ni Sakay kasi Amerikano ang nagpabitay sa kaniya. Si Bonifacio, nung pinatay si Bonifacio, masama ang loob ni Bonifacio kasi kapwa niya Pilipino. Namnamin ninyo na lang ‘yung sinabi ko,” he added.

(It’s like this— when Sakay was executed, he felt proud because it was the Americans who had him executed. But when Bonifacio was killed, he felt betrayed because it was done by his fellow Filipinos. Just reflect on what I said.)

Padilla arrived at the Department of Justice on Friday to personally attend the preliminary investigation into the obstruction of justice complaint filed against him. The charge stems from his involvement in escorting Dela Rosa out of the Senate premises in May, at a time when the latter was already facing an ICC arrest warrant.

The PNP has formed a dedicated task force to locate Dela Rosa. Meanwhile, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla has offered a P50-million bounty for anyone who can provide information leading to the senator's capture.
Since then, law enforcement agencies have repeatedly urged Dela Rosa to surrender.
However, Padilla said he will not call on his fellow senator to surrender to the ICC, citing the absence of a local court-issued arrest warrant.

“Sumuko kanino, sa dayuhan? Ay hindi… Kahit naman ako kung ICC ‘to hindi ako susuko. Bakit ako susuko don? Right 'yan ni Bato. Right niya ’yan, wala naman akong nakitang warrant of arrest na local. Walang court na humahanap sa kaniya, dayuhan to. Hay nako uminit ang ulo ko ah.”

(Surrender to whom? To a foreigner? Absolutely not… Even if it were me, if it’s the ICC, I wouldn't surrender either. Why would I surrender to them? That is Bato's right. articles.title: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of incitement
articles.summary: The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, was acquitted of the more serious charge of treason.

blocks.text: Tanzania's main opposition leader, Tundu Lissu, has been found guilty of incitement in a case that has raised concerns about political freedoms in the East African country.
The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, was convicted over remarks he made while campaigning for electoral reforms ahead of the disputed 2025 general election.
A panel of three judges at the High Court in Dar es Salaam acquitted him of the more serious charge of treason.
Lissu, who leads the opposition Chadema party, has consistently denied the charges, describing the prosecution as politically motivated.
Treason is among Tanzania's most serious offences and can carry the death penalty.
He has leave to appeal at the Court of Appeal - the country's highest court.

President Samia Suluhu Hassan won the October 2025 election with 98% of the vote - a result the opposition dismissed the result as a "mockery" of democracy as her two main challengers, including Lissu, were excluded.
Her government has repeatedly denied targeting its opponents.
The Chadema leader was arrested six months before the poll, shortly after launching a campaign demanding changes to the electoral system under the slogan "No Reforms, No Election".
Prosecutors accused him of making statements intended to incite the public to disrupt the election and threaten the government.
They argued that his remarks, which were also circulated online, amounted to treason.
But Lissu, a lawyer who represented himself during the trial, maintained that his comments were part of a legitimate political campaign for constitutional and electoral reform.
He argued that prosecutors had taken his statements out of context and failed to prove that he had committed any crime.
Some of the demands raised by Chadema were:

items: Electoral commissioners should be independently appointed (not by the president)
Police should allow all parties to campaign free of intimidation
Government-appointed district chiefs should no longer act as returning officers
Party agents should be able to observe counting without harassment
It should be possible to challenge presidential election results in court.

blocks.text: During his time in remand custody at Dar es Salaam's Ukonga Prison, Lissu went on hunger strike twice for brief periods when he said he was not allowed access to his lawyers or relatives. He also complained that guards listened to what should have been private consultations his lawyers.
These allegations have been denied by the prison authorities.
His case has attracted international attention, with rights groups expressing concern about the treatment of opposition politicians and the shrinking space for political dissent in Tanzania.
Last year's election was followed by widespread protests and a violent security crackdown that left at least 500 people dead, according to an official inquiry.
Opposition groups have said the death toll was much higher and demanded an independent investigation.
The government has defended its handling of the unrest and rejected accusations of widespread political repression.

Samia, 66, has insisted the election was fair and transparent and blamed foreigners for the unrest, saying it was part of a plot to overthrow her. She has set up another commission to inquiry to identify those behind the violence.

Lissu has long been one of Tanzania's most outspoken critics of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party, which, along with its predecessor Tanu, has dominated the country's politics since independence.
He first became an MP in 2010, representing a constituency near his birth place in Singida, 320km (200 miles) north-west of the capital, Dodoma.
In September 2017, the Chadema politician narrowly survived an assassination attempt when gunmen sprayed his vehicle with bullets outside his home in Dodoma.
He was shot multiple times and underwent extensive medical treatment abroad.
The attack, whose perpetrators have never been brought to justice, forced him to spend years outside Tanzania.
He returned to contest the 2020 presidential election against the late President John Magufuli, but lost in a vote that the opposition alleged was marred by widespread irregularities.
Lissu subsequently returned to exile before coming back to Tanzania in 2023, following President Samia's decision to lift a ban on opposition political rallies.
His return was initially seen as a sign of renewed political openness after years of restrictions under Magufuli, who died in office in 2021.
But relations between the government and the opposition deteriorated as the country approached the 2025 election.
Lissu became Chadema's national chairman in January 2025 and intensified his demands for electoral reforms.
His conviction is likely to deepen concerns about the state of democracy in Tanzania.
Last week, rights group Amnesty International accused the government of continuing its crackdown following the election and "weaponising counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear".
The authorities did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
articles.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

image.caption: Most major European markets fell more than 1%, with media, healthcare and retail stocks leading the declines.Image: REUTERS

blocks.text: European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.
Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.
How have European markets reacted?

The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week. Most major European markets fell more than 1%, with media, healthcare and retail stocks leading the declines.
European markets had previously weathered the week's turbulence better than their Asian and US counterparts because of their more limited exposure to AI stocks.
Earlier, Japanese and South Korean shares tumbled after a massive selloff in tech stocks on Wall Street the previous day.

Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.5% in early trade, while Seoul's tech-heavy Kospi index slid as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index was also down more than 8%.
Asian tech giants including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) have borne the brunt of the artificial intelligence-related selloff.
Samsung plunged nearly 10% while SK Hynix slid over 11%.
Chip-related shares in Japan also took a beating, with Tokyo Electron stock trading down around 9% and Kioxia shedding 13%.
Data centers face backlash from US communities
What's behind the stock rout on Wall Street?
US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.
The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending plans and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.
The results of the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats seize control of both houses of US Congress, added to the concerns.

A number of Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing artificial intelligence development and promised to stop or pause the construction of data centers amid growing public opposition to such projects.
"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift ​in sentiment," Michael McCarthy, chief executive for Australia and New Zealand at online brokerage Moomoo, told the Reuters news agency.

"Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that shows up in the market ​by huge swings in either direction," he said. "That's what we appear to have had — and last night's emphatic sell-down suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in."

articles.title: Rodil Zalameda takes oath as 28th Supreme Court Chief Justice
articles.summary: Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda took his oath on Friday as the new Supreme Court Chief Justice, succeeding outgoing Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who retired on the same day.

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 5:21pm
Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda took his oath on Friday as the new Supreme Court Chief Justice, succeeding outgoing Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who retired on the same day.
Assuming his post as the 28th Chief Justice of the Philippines, Zalameda took his oath alongside his family before Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen.
Meanwhile, the ceremonial turnover of the gavel was administered by Gesmundo, according to a report by Super Radyo dzBB reporter Christian Maño.
Leonen was one of his four rivals for the position, who also included Associate Justice Benjamin Caguioa, Associate Justice Japar Dimaampao, and Associate Justice Jose Midas Marquez.
Malacañang announced Zalameda’s appointment on Thursday, citing his extensive judicial experience across several administrations. Palace said it remains confident in the Judiciary’s impartiality.
It can be recalled that Zalameda penned the SC decision that overturned the graft conviction of former First Lady Imelda Marcos.

He also authored the decision granting a writ of amparo in favor of former Bayan Muna lawmaker Siegfred Deduro, which recognized that red-tagging and guilt by association threaten a person’s right to life, liberty, or security.
Prior to this, Zalameda was appointed as an SC associate justice by then-President Rodrigo Duterte on August 6, 2019.
He also served as an associate justice of the Court of Appeals for 11 years and as the chairperson of its 17th Division.
Zalameda previously served as a branch clerk for the Makati Regional Trial Court.

The new SC chief justice obtained his Bachelor of Laws degree at Ateneo de Manila University in 1987 under an academic scholarship grant. He passed the Bar examinations in 1988. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Ombudsman: 79 flood control-related cases filed in courts
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has filed with Philippine courts 79 criminal cases related to the multi-billion peso flood control corruption scandal, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said Friday.

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 5:21pm
The Office of the Ombudsman has filed with Philippine courts 79 criminal cases related to the multi-billion peso flood control corruption scandal, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said Friday.
Remulla said that of this number, 75 were filed with the Sandiganbayan while the other four with local courts.

"The ongoing flood control charges include two plunder [cases] which is non-bailable, 22 cases of malversation of public funds, which is also non-bailable because the amount [involved] is above P8.8 million, and 55 violations of Republic Act 3019, the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act," Remulla said in a press conference.

"For flood control, [the amount of projects involved in cases pending] before the court now is P10.78 billion. Remember, there's a much bigger amount involved, but we are working with the evidence that we have so far," Remulla added.
Out of the 79 cases, 67 persons are accused, including the following:

items: 1 senator
1 former senator
4 congressmen
1 former congressman
1 former secretary of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
39 DPWH personnel
9 contractors
2 congressional staff
9 private individuals

blocks.text: Further, Remulla said Ombudsman prosecutors have filed 57 non-flood control cases involving 138 respondents.
These 57 cases, Remulla said, involve P13 billion worth of public funds.
The 138 respondents in non-flood control cases include:

items: 78 elected officials
42 DPWH personnel
9 contractors
9 private individuals

blocks.text: "What are the schemes of corruption they are doing? In right-of-way [cases], they fake or falsify land ownership and supporting documents to claim government compensation for right-of-way. These are the ones affected by public infrastructure. Outdated property valuations are also used to inflate compensation claims," Remulla said.

"There are also ghost projects that come out, [the] withdrawing or spending public funds for projects that supposedly do not exist, or releasing funds without the required disbursement vouchers, receipts and other supporting documents," Remulla added. — VDV, GMA News

articles.summary:
Hoax bomb threats targeted commercial flights this week leaving at least 35 planes searched or diverted

Airlines and airports across Europe are on high alert after a wave of hoax…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 26m agoMorning opening: European skies on high alert after hoax bomb threats this week

blocks.text: Morning opening: European skies on high alert after hoax bomb threats this week

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa
Airlines and airports across Europe are on high alert after a wave of hoax bomb threats targeted commercial flights this week, leaving at least 35 planes searched or diverted.
Authorities will be hoping to see a quieter day today after yesterday’s disruptions.
But one of the incidents yesterday remains under closer scrutiny.

An Aer Lingus pilot who was flying from Dublin to Rome when the plane was diverted to the Évreux military base after a bomb threat is facing scrutiny from the French authorities after reportedly insisting on landing at a civilian airport.

blocks.caption: An Aer Lingus aircraft which was heading from Dublin to Rome and has been rerouted and escorted by military aircraft after a suspected bomb threat at Evreux-Fauville Air Base. Photograph: Guillaume Saligot/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Évreux’s public prosecutor, Rémi Coutin, told ICI Normandie that the pilot’s apparent initial refusal to land where instructed prompted the French military to scramble two fighter jets to intercept the aircraft.
The pilot and his co-pilot will be questioned to “understand what happened,” Coutin said, stressing that he could bring charges for refusing to cooperate with authorities.
In a statement to the Guardian, Aer Lingus backed the pilot, however, saying he and the crew acted “impeccably and thoroughly professional throughout” the incident.

“Safety and the care of our passengers is Aer Lingus’ top priority and this was upheld professionally by the captain and crew of the aircraft throughout in what were very challenging circumstances,” the airline said.
Elsewhere, we are expecting an update on the Belgian government as prime minister Bart De Wever meets King Philippe to discuss next steps after the collapse of budget negotiations.
Pope Leo is also off to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in his first overseas trip since his lung surgery last month.
I will bring you all the updates here.
It’s Friday, 6 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.
